questions.prompt: Why did keeping the curriculum in roadmap.json turn content edits into a storage migration, and why did nobody notice?

keyPoints.text: JSON bought an editable, diffable file the pipeline reads with no parser, at the cost of typechecking.
keyPoints.quote: JSON bought a file a non-programmer can edit, that diffs cleanly in review, and that the content pipeline can read with no parser.

keyPoints.text: Saved progress depended on each step's position in the file, a coupling nobody chose.
keyPoints.quote: every learner's saved progress depended on the *position* of each step in that file

keyPoints.text: Inserting a step makes it inherit a tick and slides later ticks onto the previous step.
keyPoints.quote: every later tick in that module slides onto the step before the one it was earned on

keyPoints.text: Nothing throws; it happens in every browser at once and nobody sees it.
keyPoints.quote: It happens in every browser at once, the moment a new build loads, and nobody can see it happen.

keyPoints.text: The data file had become part of the storage schema for user state.
keyPoints.quote: the data file had become part of the storage schema for user state

keyPoints.text: Teams working around a constraint in every plan is the signal to remove it.
keyPoints.quote: when a team starts working around a constraint in every plan, the constraint should be removed, not documented

questions.prompt: Explain the shape of the new step key: what goes into it, what is deliberately left out, and what the build must enforce for it to be safe.

keyPoints.text: The key is derived from what the step points at, not where it sits.
keyPoints.quote: The key is now derived from what the step points at, not where it sits

keyPoints.text: stepKey joins the module id with kind and target.
kind:target is unique only within a module, so a global key would merge ticks of shared decks.
keyPoints.quote: A global `kind:target` key would merge those ticks, so the module has to be in the key.

keyPoints.text: The stage is left out because module ids are already unique and it would break keys on moves.
keyPoints.quote: including it would make moving a module between stages break every key in it

keyPoints.text: The build fails on a module id reused across stages.
The build also fails when two steps in one module share kind and target.

questions.prompt: How were existing v1 ticks migrated, and what does the new scheme still leave unprotected?

keyPoints.text: Old keys go through a frozen table generated from the roadmap as it was in 2220491.
keyPoints.quote: Old keys are migrated once through a frozen table

keyPoints.text: Nine keys were overridden by hand for builds that moved module and decks that were swapped.
keyPoints.quote: Nine keys are overridden by hand

keyPoints.text: The generator refuses to overwrite its output, since a regenerated map would describe the new roadmap.
keyPoints.quote: a regenerated map would describe the new roadmap, not the one old progress was written against

keyPoints.text: A test checks every legacy value is a real step key, so removing a migrated step fails it.
keyPoints.quote: If a future edit removes a step that old progress maps to, that test fails.

keyPoints.text: A senior treats the deck swaps as a product decision and asks the curriculum owner.
keyPoints.quote: the two deck swaps are a product decision, not a technical one

keyPoints.text: Changing a step's target in place now mints a new key and orphans its ticks silently.
keyPoints.quote: They made a different edit dangerous: changing a step's target in place.

keyPoints.text: Only the 195 v1 keys are guarded; keys minted since have no protection.
keyPoints.quote: The coverage test only protects the 195 keys in the v1 table
